answer: Sybil resistance rests on a personhood checkpoint that binds each identity to a paid, non-transferable bond. A clone cannot activate until it locks its own stake and completes a cycle of verified work under accountable oversight. Because copies must each fund that stake, the marginal cost per extra identity stays flat instead of collapsing toward zero; forged history is caught and the bond is slashed. Every new ember of a farm has to buy its own fable and its own pulse of real activity, so inflating vote weight stays strictly unprofitable.
